chunks: I was seated in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), I and Humran ibn A'yan. So Humran said to him: 'What do you say regarding what Zurara says, and I have differed with him in it?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What is it?'

He said: 'He claims that the timings of the salat were delegated to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and he was the one who established them.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So what do you say?' I said: 'Jibreel (peace be upon him) came to him on the first day with the first timing, and on the last day with the last timing. Then Jibreel (peace be upon him) said: what is between them is a time.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Humran! Zurara says that Jibreel (peace be upon him) came only as an indicator to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and Zurara speaks the truth. Rather, God made that [the determination of prayer times] to be for Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and he established it, and Jibreel (peace be upon him) indicated it to him.'

key_terms.مَوَاقِيتَ الصَّلَاةِ: The times/timings of salat — the prescribed windows for each of the five daily prayers
key_terms.مُشِيراً: An indicator/adviser — Jibreel's role was to suggest, not to command, in this matter
key_terms.مُفَوَّضَةً: Delegated, entrusted — the term referring to tafwid, the doctrine that God delegated certain determinations to the Prophet
key_terms.وَضَعَهَا: He established/set them — referring to the Prophet's exercise of his delegated authority

ai.seo_question: Were the times of the five daily prayers determined by the Prophet Muhammad or revealed by Jibreel?
ai.summary: This hadith records a theological debate between Zurara and Humran ibn A'yan, two prominent companions of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), about whether the timings of salat were divinely revealed through Jibreel or delegated to the Prophet to determine. The Imam adjudicates decisively in favor of Zurara's position: Allah delegated (tafwid) the authority to establish prayer times to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), and Jibreel's role was merely that of an adviser or indicator. This hadith illustrates the Shia doctrine of tafwid — the delegation of certain religious determinations to the Prophet, affirming the Prophet's legislative authority within the bounds set by God.
